question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{x}{2})) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{x}{2})) \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{x}{2})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {(\frac{x}{2})}^{′} \\  & =6\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+1}}\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
